import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 592

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/592](https://www.erdosproblems.com/592)
-/

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos592

universe u

/--
Determine which countable ordinals $β$ have the property that, if $α = \omega^β$, then in any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_592 (β : Ordinal.{u}) : β.card ≤ ℵ₀ →
    OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ β) (ω ^ β) 3 ↔ (answer(sorry) : Ordinal.{u} → Prop) β := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add condition by Galvin and Larson.

end Erdos592

findings.description: The countability condition has the wrong scope in lines 36–37. Lean elaborates the statement as `∀ β, ((β.card ≤ ℵ₀ → R β) ↔ A β)`, where `R β` is the Ramsey property and `A` is the answer predicate, rather than `∀ β, β.card ≤ ℵ₀ → (R β ↔ A β)`. Consequently, every uncountable ordinal must satisfy `A`, independently of its Ramsey property. The countable cases agree, but the specifications of the answer predicate are not equivalent: `A β := β.card ≤ ℵ₀ ∧ R β` satisfies the intended bounded classification and fails the actual statement at `β = (ℵ₁ : Cardinal).ord`. This separation was proved in the scratch file without using any conjecture theorem or sorry axiom.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/592 and its LaTeX source https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/592 ask to “Determine which countable ordinals” β satisfy the red/blue Ramsey property for α = ω^β. Countability restricts the ordinals being classified; the source does not require the answer predicate to accept every uncountable ordinal.
findings.suggested_fix: Parenthesize the equivalence so that countability guards the whole classification: `theorem erdos_592 (β : Ordinal.{u}) : β.card ≤ ℵ₀ → (OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ β) (ω ^ β) 3 ↔ (answer(sorry) : Ordinal.{u} → Prop) β) := by sorry`. Equivalently, move countability into a theorem hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: The Ramsey subexpression encodes edge colourings using complementary simple graphs on `α.ToType`. The red target is specified by order type, while the blue target is specified by cardinality 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `α.ToType` has order type α, and equality `typeLT s = β` is equivalent to an order isomorphism between s and `β.ToType`. Complementary graphs assign exactly one of the two colours to each unordered pair of distinct vertices. A well-ordered set has cardinality 3 exactly when its order type is 3. The scratch file proves these facts and the equivalence between `OrdinalCardinalRamsey α β 3` and the single-red-graph formulation with a complementary blue clique of order type 3. This validates the Ramsey encoding, separately from the countability-scope defect.
